A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same position paper and empirical study. All 12 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original analyses of anthropomorphic language in arXiv and ACL abstracts, including temporal trends and differences across NLP subfields.

after.justification: Section 3 retains the original corpus analyses and adds a Fightin' Words analysis identifying verbs associated with high and low AnthroScore sentences.

M1.justification: The defined RoBERTa-based AnthroScore procedure and binary indicator for an abstract containing any positively scored sentence remain unchanged. The added lexical diagnostic does not revise a proposed model or training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both analyze over 200,000 computer-science arXiv abstracts from 2023–2024 and over 50,000 ACL abstracts from 2007–2022. The new lexical analysis uses the existing data; newly cited benchmarks are not evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline algorithms against a proposed method. Added discussions of Dynabench and Chatbench in Section 4.3 are literature examples, not new experimental comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds a lexical comparison between sentences with AnthroScore >1 and <-1. Its Figure 1 caption also changes the abstract criterion from at least one to >1 anthropomorphic sentence, although the formula and prose retain at least one; the plotted aggregation is therefore ambiguous.

E4.justification: The new Section 3 score-sensitivity analysis examines which verbs distinguish high and low AnthroScore sentences, probing lexical drivers and potential metric biases. v1 has no corresponding diagnostic.

E5.justification: v2 introduces weighted log-odds ratios and z-score-based lexical comparisons. Both versions retain 95% confidence intervals on prevalence plots, without changes to reported seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: The arXiv curves change substantially: v1 Figure 2 agrees with reported increases of approximately 34% to 40% for all papers and 40% to 48% for LLM papers; v2 Figure 1 instead plots roughly 12–17% and 19–30%, respectively, while retaining the old prose. These are changed reported results with unresolved aggregation settings. v2 also adds high- and low-AnthroScore verb rankings.

T1.justification: The log-probability ratio and binary abstract-level definition remain mathematically equivalent. Explicit pronoun sets in v2 restate the earlier prose; equation renumbering and reformatted assumption headings introduce no new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central position and three contributions: increasing anthropomorphic terminology, a framework covering five lifecycle assumptions, and complementary non-anthropomorphic research directions. The more explicit balanced framing reiterates qualifications already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges terminology as an imperfect proxy for anthropomorphic thinking. It also specifies when anthropomorphism constrains research and expands discussion of interface usability, public communication, and misconceptions about AI agency.

D1.justification: For the added sensitivity analysis, v2 documents the high/low score cutoffs and weighted-log-odds/z-score procedure. Existing corpus sourcing and model information remain, without new code access, hardware, or runtime disclosures.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on Fightin' Words, dynamic and interactive evaluation, and framing and public perceptions. It removes the DeepSeek reasoning example and associated citation. These changes extend the supporting literature without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, analytical framing, and alternative views are revised; assumptions become subsection titles, and public-impact discussion is incorporated into Section 6. The overall section sequence and most lifecycle case-study prose remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. The iceberg illustration is replaced by a detailed framework summary table, and v1 Figures 2–4 become a compact three-panel Figure 1. The subfield chart is transposed and relabeled, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a useful lexical diagnostic, framework summary, and explicit proxy limitation. However, v1's arXiv figure agrees with its reported percentages, whereas v2 retains those percentages alongside substantially lower curves and a conflicting sentence-count criterion. This unexplained mismatch weakens a central empirical contribution and outweighs the limited gains, although the qualitative trends and main position remain intact.
